first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and activation is down 6%. Memory_31 showed that signup simplification improved SMB activation, and memory_86 demonstrated that shortened onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value. These are directly addressable levers for the current decline. Verifying both will confirm the magnitude and durability of the onboarding effect before applying it. While promotional_pricing appears relevant to competitive pressure, competing on price erodes margin and creates acquisition quality risk. Enterprise_sales_assist is higher-touch but targets a different segment. Referral incentives work well for retention but don't address the immediate activation and onboarding completion problem. Activation_messaging (memory_91) is a useful supporting lever but secondary to fixing the funnel friction. A simplified onboarding intervention should restore baseline activation quickly while creating sustainable long-term value through improved time-to-value and user experience.

final.rationale: Archive verification confirms both signals. Memory_31 showed signup simplification +15% signups, +9% activation, +4% qualified revenue on SMB (with -1% retention risk, acceptable). Memory_86 showed shortened onboarding +13% completion, -2.1 days time-to-value, +3% retention lift. Current state: onboarding completion down 4% QoQ, activation down 6% QoQ. A standard_experiment applying simplified onboarding directly addresses both metrics while building on proven intervention. The retention upside from memory_86 and qualified revenue lift from memory_31 suggest sustainable value creation, not short-term gain at cost. Competitor pricing pressure remains, but competing on friction reduction (rather than price) protects margin and creates defensible differentiation. This intervention targets the right lever with high confidence and measurable downstream quality signals.
